incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 of New Zealand, particularly ss 10-17 (registration and effect of registration), s 18 (constitution), ss 41-47 (share capital), ss 122-127 (director requirements), ss 131-137 (director duties), ss 200-203 (registered office), and the Financial Reporting Act 2013 (reporting obligations).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Online Registration of a Company application submitted through the New Zealand Companies Register (equivalent to a statutory application under s 12 of the Companies Act 1993)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum issued or paid-up capital exists for a New Zealand International Company limited by shares; no blocked escrow account is required. Share capital may be denominated in any currency, with no par value or with a par value, and consideration may consist of money, property, or services approved by the directors.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [●] INTERNATIONAL COMPANY LIMITED; (incorporated under the Companies Act 1993 of New Zealand). RESOLVED, as follows: 1. Adoption of Constitution. The Constitution presented to and reviewed by the Board is approved and adopted as the constitutive document of the Company, and the Directors are directed to ensure a copy is kept at the Company's registered office and made available to every shareholder and director in accordance with sections 16 and 18 of the Companies Act 1993. 2. Registered Office and Address. The registered office of the Company is fixed at [●], New Zealand. The Directors are authorized to file all notices of registered office and any subsequent changes with the New Zealand Companies Office, and to maintain the statutory records, registers, and minute book at that address. 3. Subscription and Allotment of Share Capital. The authorized share capital of the Company shall be such number of ordinary shares as the Directors may resolve; the subscribers named in the incorporation application and each person listed in the shareholders' schedule shall subscribe for the number of shares set opposite their respective names. The Directors are authorized to accept the subscriptions and to allot and issue such shares, to record the allotment in the share register, and to issue share certificates as appropriate. All subscription moneys shall be paid to the Company's bank account and held for the benefit of the Company. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. [●] is appointed sole director of the Company, and [●] is appointed company secretary (where applicable). Each officer shall be and hereby is authorized to exercise all powers and discretions conferred by the Companies Act 1993 and the Constitution, including the power to convene meetings, maintain minutes, and execute documents on behalf of the Company. 5. Banking Arrangements. The Directors are authorized to open bank accounts in the name of the Company with [●] Bank, and to appoint the sole director as the sole signing officer; alternatively, the Board may require any two Directors or a Director and the Company Secretary to sign cheques and electronic payment instructions. Bank mandates and specimen signatures are approved. 6. General Delegation and Filing. The Directors are directed to complete all statutory filings, including the notification to the Inland Revenue Department, and any applications for banking and business registrations, and to do all things necessary to implement these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - Companies Register online (Name Search and Reserve Name services), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: On the Companies Office portal, conduct a full-text exact and similar name availability search. If the proposed name is unavailable, too similar, or misleading under the Companies Act 1993, select an alternative name and search again. Reserve the chosen name electronically for up to 20 working days by paying the applicable reservation fee, and download the reservation reference. For an International Company, include the required company suffix (for example 'Limited' or an approved abbreviation) and obtain a signed consent letter from any individual or entity whose name appears in the company name. After the reservation is issued, preserve the reference number and use it when completing the online incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and at least two alternative names
Director's full legal name, date of birth, and residential address
Consent letter from any individual or entity whose name is used in the company name
Power of attorney or agent authorization letter (if a registered agent is used)
Name reservation fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is queried by the Registrar as objectionable or too similar, a written submission addressing the Registrar's objections may be filed within 10 working days with the Companies Office, including evidence of consent or distinctiveness; if the reservation lapses, re-apply in the next available slot or elect a revised name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Filing of Incorporation Application and Constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - online incorporation application through the Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the New Zealand Companies Office online incorporation application through the Companies Register. Enter the reserved company name, the full legal name and date of birth and residential address for each director and shareholder, the New Zealand registered office address, and an address for service. Indicate whether a constitution is adopted; if none, the default rules in the Companies Act 1993 apply. Attach the certified consent to act as director, proof of identity and residential address for every director, and the name reservation reference. Verify that at least one director (if a natural person) resides in New Zealand or in an eligible enforcement jurisdiction; otherwise, consider enlisting a local agent. Submit the application and pay the official filing fee online. The Registrar checks the application and, if compliant, issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
required_dossiers: Completed online incorporation application
Constitution (if adopted; otherwise default statutory rules apply)
Consent to act as director for each proposed director
Certified passport or national identity card for each director
Proof of residential address for each director (not older than 3 months)
Name reservation reference number
Registered office address and address for service details
Payment of official filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended, respond to the Companies Office query notice within the stated deadline by filing corrected consent forms, identity evidence, or a certified statutory declaration; a rejected application may be resubmitted after rectification and payment of any applicable re-filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Statutory Records, and Banking Mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company; New Zealand Companies Office (for registry updates); selected commercial bank in New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or circulate a written resolution signed by all directors. Adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution described in this dossier, including the approval of the constitution, fixed registered office, allotment of shares, appointment of director(s), company secretary (if desired), and the bank mandate. Minute the resolution and enter the allotment in the share register and the officer appointments in the director and secretary registers. Issue share certificates to each subscriber. Contact the selected bank with the certificate of incorporation, NZBN, board resolution, certified director identification, and proof of the registered office address; complete the bank's customer due diligence and AML/CFT questionnaires and declare the beneficial ownership. Once approved, collect the bank's written confirmation of accounts and signing authority.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
First board resolution (signed board minutes or written resolution)
Constitution of the Company
Register of directors, register of shareholders, and register of charges
Director identification and proof of residential address
Bank account application forms and AML/CFT due diligence questionnaire
Beneficial ownership and source-of-funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open an account, provide enhanced due diligence by explaining the source of funds and economic purpose, or select another licensed bank; if the Companies Office flags an officer disqualification, immediately correct the appointment to a compliant director and file the change of director particulars online.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD); New Zealand Companies Office; New Zealand Customs Service (if the Company imports goods)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the first month of incorporation, file the company's first annual return details and ensure the Companies Office registers are current. Register with the Inland Revenue Department in myIR to obtain an IRD number; assess whether GST registration is compulsory because New Zealand taxable supplies are or are expected to exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period; if so, file Form GST 101. For a non-resident-owned International Company, evaluate whether non-resident withholding tax or supplementary returns apply. If the Company will import goods for Amazon FBA, open a client code with New Zealand Customs and obtain the importer customs client code; if hiring staff, register as an employer for PAYE. No industrial license is required for this ISIC 4791 online-retail classification.
required_dossiers: NZBN certificate
Certificate of Incorporation
IRD number application and myIR activation details
GST registration form (if applicable)
Details of shareholders and directors for tax-residency classification
Statement of online sales and cross-border supply model
New Zealand Customs client code application (if goods will be imported)
Employer registration form (if employees will be engaged)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD asserts tax avoidance or residency concerns, submit a technical position paper citing the Companies Act and applicable double-tax agreement; apply for administrative remission of late filing penalties if the delay was caused by incorrect official advice and document the correspondence with the IRD.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the business is classified under ISIC 4791 (Retail sale via the internet) and does not undertake manufacturing, chemical processing, physically licensed assembly, or warehousing operations in New Zealand.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating license is required for an online marketplace / Amazon FBA general retail business.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - environmental regulatory agencies are not engaged for this purely digital retail classification.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable (Category 999: no physical installation). The activity generates no industrial discharges or emissions; if a future distribution facility is established in New Zealand, an appropriate assessment under the Resource Management Act 1991 may become applicable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable: zero wastewater, zero point-source VOC emissions, no hazardous waste stream. If ancillary warehousing is later operated, the operator must comply with any Resource Management Act discharge permit conditions and the National Environmental Standards for wastewater and air quality.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for pure online retail; however, any occupied office or warehouse must hold a current Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) from the territorial authority, a fire evacuation scheme approved by Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ), and workplace induction and emergency procedures under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015. No civil defense industry clearance is triggered by the ISIC 4791 online-retail activity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue (Inland Revenue Department / Te Tari Taake), New Zealand; online portal: myIR (https://myir.ird.govt.nz)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Cook Islands International Company (CK IC) is a non-resident foreign company for New Zealand tax purposes. It is required to obtain a New Zealand IRD number only where it derives New Zealand-source income subject to income tax, or where it must register (or elects to register) for GST. Procedure for a non-resident entity: (1) assemble certified copies of the Cook Islands certificate of incorporation, the international company's constitution, register of directors and shareholders, and underlying beneficial ownership records; (2) lodge the prescribed non-resident company IRD number application (form IR596) or apply online through myIR, either directly or through an appointed New Zealand tax agent; (3) if GST registration is required or voluntary, complete form IR372 (or the online GST registration in myIR) indicating the estimated 12-month turnover of taxable supplies in New Zealand, the commencement date of the taxable activity, New Zealand bank account details, and the nature of the cross-border e-commerce operations; (4) Inland Revenue normally issues the IRD number and, where applicable, the GST registration number within 10 to 20 working days. Where the CK IC sells exclusively through Amazon FBA as a marketplace seller to New Zealand consumers, it may have no direct GST registration obligation because Amazon, as the approved marketplace operator, is liable to collect GST on low-value goods (value not exceeding NZD 1,000) under sections 60B and 60C of the GST Act 1985.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: the CK IC is a Cook Islands International Company resident and incorporated in the Cook Islands, exempt from Cook Islands income tax on offshore-sourced income under the International Companies Act; for New Zealand tax purposes it is a non-resident foreign company taxable only on New Zealand-source income or income attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment (PE), with foreign-source income fully outside the New Zealand income tax net absent a PE. If Amazon FBA inventory is not warehoused in New Zealand and no dependent agent operates in New Zealand, the CK IC has no New Zealand income tax registration or filing obligation; if a NZ PE is created (e.g., NZ fulfillment centre or local staff), entity-level taxation would apply to attributable profits at the 28% corporate rate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand has no US-style check-the-box regime. Statutory elections relevant to a non-resident IC include: (i) voluntary GST registration for a non-resident supplier whose New Zealand taxable supplies are below the NZD 60,000 threshold; (ii) election to treat associated companies as a GST group under section 55 of the GST Act 1985; (iii) election to zero-rate supplies of a going concern or land; (iv) for New Zealand-resident close companies, the Look-Through Company (LTC) election (section HB 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007) which confers fiscal transparency - unavailable to a non-resident IC; (v) elections and deemed elections under the hybrid and branch mismatch rules in Subpart FH of the Income Tax Act 2007 (including the imported mismatch 'CBC report' concession); and (vi) foreign-currency realisation timing elections for tax accounting. None of these elections alter the fundamental non-resident, offshore exemption character of the CK IC.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) - a broad-based, single-stage value-added tax on consumption administered under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; no separate state or municipal sales/use taxes exist in New Zealand.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period (GST Act 1985, s 51). For non-resident suppliers of remote services (including digital services) and for non-resident sellers of low-value imported goods (each item not exceeding NZD 1,000) sold through an electronic marketplace, registration is mandatory once the NZD 60,000 threshold is exceeded, and voluntary below it. Where an approved marketplace operator (e.g., Amazon) is liable for GST on the low-value goods under sections 60B-60C of the GST Act 1985, the underlying non-resident seller (CK IC) is not required to register solely by reason of those supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory tax-authority API clearance, or digital stamping regime exists in New Zealand. E-invoicing operates on the voluntary Peppol BIS 3.0 standard under the trans-Tasman e-Invoicing initiative, with certified access points exchanging standard e-invoices. From 1 April 2025, suppliers invoicing New Zealand central government agencies must deliver e-invoices via a certified Peppol access point. Inland Revenue does not pre-approve or digitally stamp invoices; GST returns and zero-rated export schedules are filed electronically via myIR, and export validation is performed through automated data matching between Inland Revenue and the New Zealand Customs Service (Trade Single Window).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under sections 11 and 11A of the GST Act 1985, a supply of goods is zero-rated when the supplier exports the goods from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply (or such extended time as the Commissioner allows) and obtains the statutory export evidence. Goods sold through an Amazon FBA model are zero-rated where the goods are removed from New Zealand for supply to an overseas buyer. Services (including marketplace facilitation, advertising, logistics software and fulfilment services) are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply and are not performed in connection with New Zealand land or goods, or where they are 'remote services' consumed outside New Zealand (s 11A). To sustain the zero rate, the supplier must retain evidence that the goods left New Zealand (customs and carrier records) and that the exported goods were paid for (foreign exchange receipts), and for services, evidence of the customer's non-resident status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export entry validated in the New Zealand Customs Trade Single Window)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank or payment-rail evidence of receipt of foreign currency for the exported goods)
Carrier shipping manifest / tracking report demonstrating physical departure of goods from New Zealand
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue and New Zealand Customs conduct automated cross-matching of zero-rated export claims against export entries; any mismatch triggers a review and recharacterisation of the supply as taxable at 15% GST, with the tax shortfall plus use-of-money interest being assessed. A clawback also arises where goods claimed as exported are re-imported, diverted back into New Zealand, or where the 28-day export period is missed without a Commissioner extension. Civil shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 (ss 120-141) apply at 20% for lack of reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, and 150% for evasion or abusive tax positions; fraudulent export documentation attracts criminal prosecution with fines and imprisonment of up to five years. Under the Customs and Excise Act 2018, false export declarations also expose the exporter to seizure and forfeiture of the goods and additional monetary penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) and the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for conduct; the RBNZ administers the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989, and the Foreign Exchange (FE) regime is liberal. There is no New Zealand Foreign Exchange Administration; wire transactions and FX dealing are handled by registered banks and financial service providers subject to AML/CFT and FMA rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand has a floating exchange rate regime with full current account and capital account convertibility. There are no exchange controls, no restrictions on foreign currency accounts, and no approvals required for profit repatriation, dividends, or capital injections by non-residents. The only checks are AML/CFT verification by the reporting entity in the transfer chain. The NZD is freely convertible, and cross-border payments can be made without prior RBNZ approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand does not impose any statutory surrender requirements for export proceeds. Exporters may hold foreign currency earnings in NZ bank accounts or overseas without conversion or repatriation deadlines. No mandatory conversion ratio applies. Returns for statistical purposes are required only under RBNZ reporting forms (e.g., certain balance of payments reporting), but there is no surrender rule.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Multi-Currency Account (NZD, USD, CNH)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for auxiliary payment processing and cross-border collection (e.g., Airwallex, Stripe, Windcave). However, an offshore digital EMI cannot provide full corporate banking services licensed under New Zealand law, cannot take deposits, and may require registration as a financial service provider under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 if it conducts business with the New Zealand public. The CK_IC may use EMIs as settlement rail for FBA proceeds and supplier disbursements, but main treasury liquidity should be housed in a licensed New Zealand bank for credibility and regulatory clarity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand banks generally allow remote onboarding for offshore companies if the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is verifiable through passport-grade KYC and video interview. Physical presence is not a statutory mandate for CK_IC type entities, but for an International Company using a tax-exempt structure, a personal appearance of the UBO or director may be requested at the discretion of the bank's risk and compliance team. If remote opening fails, a professional introducer—NZ legal counsel or registered AML/CFT compliance officer—may appear on behalf. Physical presence materially increases approval probability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner opacity due to International Company class and offshore tax exemption
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide full UBO chart with passports, source of wealth reports, apostilled incorporation documents, register of directors, certificate of good standing, and a legal opinion from NZ counsel confirming the entity's tax-exempt status and that it is not a shell company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border receipt from Amazon marketplace and payment processors without clear underlying product flow
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply Amazon Seller Central dashboard summaries, warehouse fulfillment records (FBA shipment logs), commercial invoices to Amazon or customers, and logistics shipping documents to prove the funds arise from actual product sales.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wire transfers routed through multiple fintech aggregators causing source-of-funds ambiguity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a clear routing map: from Amazon Pay or Stripe settlement account to the CK_IC bank account, with aggregated payout reports; avoid mixing personal and business funds; maintain a ledger matching each bank inflow to an Amazon payout statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: NZD trade disbursements to Asian suppliers (particularly China/Hong Kong) triggering correspondent bank review
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain full supplier onboarding files: supplier business license or registration, contract, proforma invoice, bill of lading, and proof of actual goods shipment; use SWIFT MT103 with invoice reference; reject transshipment through unknown shell entities.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder loans or equity contributions via SWIFT MT103 from the parent or UBO account using accurate purpose codes (e.g., code 110 or LOAN for intercompany loans; code 109 or INVC for equity). New Zealand has no exchange-control permission, but the receiving bank requires a clear remittance description such as 'Intercompany capital injection / loan for working capital'. Bank will perform AML source-of-funds checks on the remitter. For amounts exceeding NZD 15,000, KYC and source-of-wealth documentation must accompany; for larger capital injections above NZD 1 million, provide board resolutions, executed loan agreement, and net-worth evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for fast, auditable supplier trade payments across borders. For larger or documentary trade purchases, a Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) is appropriate and available from tier-1 NZ banks. Amazon FBA supplier payments are normally made by MT103. ACH/payment rails are not allowed for cross-border from NZD to offshore vendor; always use SWIFT or fintech bank-featured accounts (e.g., Airwallex) for forked settlement, with beneficiary name matching the supplier operating agreement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot NZD/USD and cross-currency trades with tier-1 NZ banks
Vanilla FX forwards (up to 12-24 months) for USD and CNY exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNY via international bank desk if onshore CNY hedging is unavailable; may be used for CNH/CNY risk
Cross-currency swaps for long-term inventory funding or intercompany loan servicing
FX options (generally for wholesale investors; CK_IC may qualify as an eligible investor if it satisfies the FMCA wholesale investor test)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Act 1993, s 210) filed online via the New Zealand Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), Ministry of Business, Innovation & Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 1 month of the company's annual return date (typically the incorporation anniversary); the Registrar issues a reminder notice approximately 2 months before the due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is an offence under s 220 of the Companies Act 1993 punishable by a fine of up to NZD 500 (approx. USD 300); continued default permits the Registrar, after 20 working days' notice, to strike the company off the register under s 318 and wind up its assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the annual return; any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership must be recorded in the company's registers within 10 working days of becoming known
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Company penalties of up to NZD 10,000 (approx. USD 6,000) for failure to maintain or confirm the UBO register; knowingly providing false or omitting UBO information attracts penalties up to NZD 50,000 (approx. USD 30,000); individual directors may be jointly liable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (prepared and presented to shareholders; filed only if mandatory)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Delivered to shareholders; filed with the New Zealand Companies Office or IRD if the company is 'large' or an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Reporting Act 2013
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder delivery within 6 months of the balance date; if a mandatory filing obligation applies, delivery to the Registrar within the statutory period specified under FRA 2013 (generally 4 months for FMC reporting entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to prepare financial statements commit an offence under the FRA 2013, with fines up to NZD 10,000 (approx. USD 6,000) for small companies and up to NZD 50,000 (approx. USD 30,000) for large companies; disqualification powers may also be exercised.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (IR4/IR4NZ) including tax-exempt status confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, due 7 July (non-calculated taxpayers) or 7 April (calculated taxpayers); tax-agent and non-standard balance date extensions may apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 (initial NZD 250 and monthly increments up to NZD 1,000, approx. USD 600) plus use-of-money interest on any deficiency; material non-compliance may trigger reassessment and revocation of the tax-exempt zone status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit applies only if the company is 'large' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 (s 45): two or more of total assets exceeding NZD 60m, annual revenue exceeding NZD 30m, and more than 100 employees; or if the company is an FMC reporting entity or its constitution or shareholders require an audit. A small Amazon FBA marketplace seller will normally be exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand GAAP relies on IFRS: Tier 1 (NZ IFRS), Tier 2 (NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime), Tier 3 (NZ SA Simple Format Reporting), and Tier 4 (NZ CAS Cash-basis Simple Format). The selected framework must reflect the entity's size, public accountability, and applicable reporting requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, at the time of filing the Companies Office annual return, a director must confirm the Ultimate Beneficial Owner register is true and current. Each share transfer and any resulting UBO change must be entered in the registers within 10 working days; the Registrar may at any time demand production of the UBO register with supporting identification data, and the information must also be produced to the New Zealand Police and IRD upon lawful request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders' and Directors' Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 - 500 per year (NZD 350 - 850) for registered office and address-for-service agency services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 9,000 per year (NZD 5,000 - 15,000) if the audit threshold is triggered; typically zero for a small tax-exempt FBA company

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday under the Income Tax Act 2007. A 15% R&D tax credit is available for eligible research and development expenditure. The imputation regime prevents double taxation on distributed profits. There is no specific e-commerce or digital services tax incentive; standard corporate rate applies to Amazon FBA profits derived in or through a New Zealand permanent establishment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 - Income Tax Return for Companies; filed electronically through Inland Revenue myIR or approved tax-software (e.g., Xero, MYOB, Reckon) via the IRD e-filing interface.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (financial year ending 31 March for standard balance date; non-standard balance dates require IRD approval).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return is due no later than 7 July. For a non-standard balance date, the return must be filed by the 7th day of the fourth month after the balance date, unless a tax agent extension is granted (commonly extending to 31 March of the following year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessable income from all sources, including Amazon Marketplace gross sales (net of refunds / returns), foreign exchange gains, and other ordinary revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the company is a New Zealand tax resident, report worldwide income. If treated as a non-resident International Company, report only New Zealand-sourced income attributable to a New Zealand PE; otherwise enter zero and attach a statement of non-residence and PE analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenses incurred in deriving assessable income, including Amazon FBA fulfillment fees, advertising, freight, packaging, storage, selling commissions, and general administrative overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct expenses only to the extent they relate to the New Zealand taxable income; allocate cross-border costs in compliance with transfer pricing rules and the arm's length principle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit after statutory adjustments and depreciation. A negative amount (tax loss) may be carried forward for future offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident without a New Zealand PE, this box will normally be zero. Losses are only available to a non-resident if attributable to a New Zealand PE and subject to continuity tests.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward from earlier years utilised against the current year's taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may utilise loss carry-forwards strictly against income that is subject to New Zealand income tax (i.e., PE income). If the company is tax-exempt in its residence jurisdiction, any claimed loss in New Zealand must still satisfy the continuity and quantum (50%) ownership rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: initial NZD 250 plus NZD 50 for each additional day the return is outstanding, up to a maximum of NZD 2,500 (total maximum NZD 2,750). Interest on unpaid terminal tax at the applicable use-of-money rate accrues daily. Further shortfall penalties (20% for lack of reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for abusive tax position, 150% for evasion) may apply if the late return accompanies an understated tax liability.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% statutory Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, unless reduced under an applicable Double Tax Agreement (DTA). For a resident shareholder, resident withholding tax (RWT) may apply at 33% (or 28% for imputed dividends).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced treaty rate, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) from its tax authority and provide it to the New Zealand payer (or Inland Revenue) prior to the dividend payment. The payer must submit the IR290 (Non-Resident Withholding Tax Agreement) declaration and retain the TRC as supporting documentation. If the reduced rate is not applied at source, a refund can be claimed via an IR4R application, provided the claim is made within four years of the end of the income year. The beneficial owner must satisfy any limitation-of-benefits provision and, where required, demonstrate active trade or business to qualify for DTA relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT rates: royalties - 15%; interest - 15%. The Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) at 2% may replace the 15% NRWT on interest paid by a qualifying New Zealand borrower to a non-resident associate. DTA rates commonly reduce interest to 10% (or 0% for arm's length transactions) and royalties to 5% or 10%, depending on the treaty partner and IP character.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 1,000,000 (aggregate cross-border related-party transactions per income year) – based on Inland Revenue's administrative de minimis safe harbour. Above this threshold, contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, including a Local File and (if applicable) a Master File, is expected to be maintained.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand is not an Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) jurisdiction; the IRD instead applies the general anti-avoidance rule (Part IVA of the Income Tax Act 2007) and New Zealand's controlled foreign company (CFC) rules. An International Company classified as 'Tax_Exempt_Zone' must nevertheless demonstrate real commercial substance (e.g., local management, physical presence, payroll, contracts) in the jurisdiction in which it claims residence; otherwise the IRD may impose tax on its New Zealand-sourced income by treating it as having a PE or by challenging the structure under GAAR. For Amazon FBA sellers, maintaining warehouse inventory in New Zealand (or via third-party fulfillment) and employing local agents will create a PE, regardless of any purported tax-exempt status.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating or omitting income derived from Amazon FBA sales on the IR4 return, including concealing gross proceeds channelled through Amazon Pay, Stripe, Airwallex, or other payment rails, or falsifying supplier invoices to inflate deductible expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Sections 143A and 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994, a person convicted of tax evasion is liable to a fine of up to NZD 50,000 per charge and imprisonment for up to 5 years. Civil shortfall penalties may reach 150% of the tax underpaid. Inland Revenue may also issue a notice of assessment based on the amount actually repatriated, with compound interest accruing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorise or are knowingly party to the evasion may be prosecuted personally. Courts can issue civil restitution orders, disqualify directorial office, impose travel bans for outstanding revenue debts, and impose terms of imprisonment of up to 5 years under the Crimes Act 1961.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Amazon FBA vendor entity as a mere corporate shell with no substantive activity in the claimed tax-resident jurisdiction, while all management and control (or core business functions) are exercised in New Zealand, in order to exploit a Tax_Exempt_Zone status and avoid New Zealand corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Part IVA (GAAR) enables the Commissioner of Inland Revenue to reconstruct the taxable profit and disregard the arrangement for tax purposes. Shortfall penalties apply at 20% for unreasonable tax position, 100% for abusive tax position, or 150% for evasion. The Companies Act 1993, s 634 (fraudulent trading) may be invoked to make the company and its directors liable for debts and taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally and severally liable for company taxes under s 372 of the Companies Act 1993 if they signed false returns or allowed trading while knowing the company was insolvent. Restitution orders, travel bans, and potential imprisonment for up to 10 years under the Crimes Act for false accounting may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting customer funds through payment service providers (Amazon Pay, Stripe, Airwallex) without implementing a compliant Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) programme, including insufficient customer due diligence, absence of beneficial ownership verification, and failure to report suspicious transactions, particularly where the entity is an international company with an opaque ownership structure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, a body corporate commits an offence if it does not comply with its AML/CFT obligations; penalties include civil penalties of up to NZD 2 million per contravention and criminal fines for senior officers. Additionally, the Financial Markets Authority may issue public warning notices, and persistent non-compliance may result in the winding up of the company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior officers, including directors and beneficial owners with substantial control, may be individually fined up to NZD 300,000 and imprisoned for up to 2 years for knowingly permitting money laundering or terrorist financing. Courts may also issue banning orders against individuals from holding a directorship in any New Zealand company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring cross-border payments to related parties (e.g., inflated IP royalties or management fees) in a zero-tax or tax-exempt jurisdiction in connection with the Amazon FBA operation, while failing to maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation or using pricing inconsistent with the arm's length standard.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may adjust the taxable profit under ss GC 8–GC 14 of the Income Tax Act 2007 to reflect an arm's length outcome. A shortfall penalty of 20% (inadequate documentation) or 50% (unacceptable tax position) applies; where the transfer pricing adjustment exceeds NZD 100,000 and an arrangement is abusive, a penalty of 150% may be imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve transfer pricing documentation without exercising reasonable care may be subject to joint and several liability for the resulting shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act. If a director knew, or should have known, that the pricing was contrived and caused the company to evade tax, the court may impose personal civil liability and, for serious cases, travel bans or imprisonment.
